title: Ravenna-attributed Mass-book fragments: bounded attestations and unresolved local reception

traditions.label: Mass-book fragments attributed to Ravenna: local use unproved
traditions.scope: Four physically identified fragmentary Eucharistic-book states associated with Ravenna in scholarship or origin catalogues, including northern Italian lectionary strips whose Ravenna use is unproved. A research grouping, not one local recension or lineage.
traditions.coverage_note: None establishes a Ravenna annual Missal, continuous local use, a complete Eucharistic prayer, or a textual transition. Independent dates and origin qualifications control each witness.

sources.title: National Library of Sweden A 135a: catalogue and TEI, revision 25 August 2026
sources.inspection: Contents, physical description, origin, provenance, acquisition, license and complete TEI inspected; both S1r/S1v original images inspected. Catalogue identifies the surviving Mass formularies, one 30 x 200 mm strip, Italy/Ravenna? and first-quarter eighth-century dating based on Gamber 1958.
sources.limitations: Early provenance is unknown; Ravenna is low-certainty attribution. Image inspection verifies fragmentary physical extent and visible liturgical headings, not a complete transcription, independent palaeographic date, or local use.

sources.title: University of Wroclaw Akc. 1955/3, publication 84013 / edition 133364
sources.inspection: Whole catalogue HTML and metadata inspected, including 701-750 date, current shelfmark, same-codex relation to Stockholm A 135a and public-domain image declaration. Both original image sides in the linked complete two-canvas GLAM manifest inspected.
sources.limitations: No Ravenna place of copying or local liturgical use is established by this record. Surviving strips do not supply the missing whole codex or a complete Eucharistic prayer.

sources.title: Earlier Latin Manuscripts: CLA XI 1596, Stockholm-Wroclaw sacramentary fragments
sources.inspection: Exact shelfmarks, contents, VIII first-half (701-750) date, Northern Italian attribution, Avicenna binding provenance and script commentary inspected in the record and full 2047-row CSV export.
sources.limitations: The catalogue gives probable Northern Italy rather than Ravenna. This broader date differs from Manuscripta's 700-725 range; the stage retains both descriptions.

sources.title: Earlier Latin Manuscripts: CLA IX 1361, Stuttgart Cod. fragm. 100A
sources.inspection: Contents, VII (601-700) date, current/former shelfmarks, uncertain origin, c. 800 penitential overwrite and Constance/Weingarten provenance inspected. Complete catalogue illustration of an opening inspected; undertext is fragmentary and difficult to read.
sources.limitations: The illustration is a sample, not a complete original codex. Catalogue sacramentary-type labels disagree across sources. Ravenna use and a complete Canon have not been established.

sources.title: Earlier Latin Manuscripts: CLA III 376, Montecassino 271 [palimpsest old 2]
sources.inspection: Exact lower-layer identification, VII–VIII (680-720) date, Gregorian sacramentary-fragment contents and Italian origin inspected. Provenance identifies eleventh-century Beneventan rewriting with Gregory's Dialogues. Complete catalogue illustration of p. 84 inspected.
sources.limitations: The sample illustration and metadata do not establish every lower-text page or whole-book content. Other reused missal strata in the same present codex must remain separate. Ravenna origin remains a scholarly question.

sources.title: Andrzej Suski, Latin liturgical manuscripts surviving as palimpsests, Liturgia Sacra 29/1 (2022), 163-205
sources.inspection: Complete 43-page PDF acquired; title, abstract, bibliography, printed p. 189 items 69-71 and p. 196 item 145 inspected. Item 71 separates the early Gregorian lower layer of Montecassino 271 from two X/XI-century missals; item 145 identifies Stuttgart 100A and its editions.
sources.limitations: Catalogue descriptions are secondary evidence, not a new collation. Suski's mixed-Gelasian label for Stuttgart 100A differs from other catalogues. Listed page examples include an explicit etc., so they are not a complete denominator.

sources.title: Arthur Westwell, The Carolingian Sacramentaries of Saint-Amand (2024), chapter 1
sources.inspection: Whole book PDF acquired from institutional repository; title/rights page, p. 42, note 121 / PDF p. 68, 56 note 180, 58-62 and note 201 inspected. Discusses Montecassino 271 as a mass-prayer/reading book, the single Stockholm-Wroclaw codex, and the evidential limits of Gamber's Ravenna archetype hypothesis.
sources.limitations: Critical discussion does not independently date or locate the fragment scriptoria. No Ravenna archetype is promoted to a surviving book or historical stage. PDF figures carry separate rights.

sources.title: Earlier Latin Manuscripts, CLA IX 1334, Munich Clm 29303(1
sources.inspection: Complete record and complete delivered facsimile sample inspected; exact current shelfmark, 576–600 date and northern Italian probable origin checked against Hauke p. 187. Photograph shows first-strip verso and part of second-strip verso, with visible John/Jeremiah reading material.
sources.limitations: Sample only, not all manuscript sides, independent palaeographic judgment or Ravenna use.

sources.title: Hermann Hauke, BSB Latin fragments catalogue I (1994), pp. 91, 187
sources.inspection: Complete 477-page generated PDF acquired. Printed pp. 91 and 187 original images directly inspected. Clm 29270(8 is a ninth-century Salzburg Gospel fragment collection; Clm 29303(1 is a sixth-century northern Italian Comes duplex surviving as two strips. The old Clm 29155 c alias is not unique enough to merge the records.
sources.limitations: Catalogue identity and contents evidence, not independent palaeographic dating, Ravenna copying, local use or complete annual-book evidence.

stages.label: Stockholm-Wroclaw Gelasian Mass-prayer fragments
stages.scope: Surviving strips from a single Gelasian sacramentary: votive/live/dead/abbot-and-community Mass-prayer material identified by the Swedish catalogue. No whole-book extent is reconstructed.
stages.witness_label: Stockholm A135a and Wroclaw Akc.1955/3: one Gelasian sacramentary's fragments
stages.summary: The two institutional catalogues resolve the fragments to one codex; original images show tiny preserved parts of Mass formularies.

evidence.claim: The catalogue identifies Mass-prayer fragments and uncertain Ravenna origin; both strip sides were inspected.
A dated, shelfmarked fragment is related to A135a as the same codex.

evidence.locus: CLA XI 1596 shelfmarks, date and provenance
evidence.claim: The joint record dates the codex to 701-750 and locates it only probably in Northern Italy.

stages.limitations: Numeric bounds preserve the two catalogue ranges rather than selecting Gamber's narrow dating as settled. Not a complete Canon/anaphora, not two liturgical versions, and not an annual Ravenna Missal.
stages.reception: No Ravenna church's actual use is established. The present holdings and scholarly attribution do not establish local reception.

stages.label: Stuttgart 100A sacramentary undertext
stages.date_label: Seventh-century copying 601-700; catalogue range, not date of later overwrite
stages.scope: One surviving sacramentary palimpsest fragment beneath penitential canons. Its liturgical type is disputed across catalogues.
stages.witness_label: Stuttgart Cod.fragm.100A: sacramentary lower text beneath penitential canons
stages.summary: The exact fragment and its lower-text date are identified; later reuse and uncertain origin remain separate.

evidence.locus: CLA IX 1361 Date; Contents; Origin and Provenance; Notes
evidence.claim: The record identifies 100A, its seventh-century sacramentary lower text, c. 800 overwrite and later custody.
A distinct shelfmarked liturgical palimpsest is catalogued with its edition loci.

stages.limitations: A documented physical fragment attestation only. Type labels Leonine-form, mixed Gelasian and pre-Hadrian Gregorian conflict; neither local recension nor complete Eucharistic prayer is established.
stages.reception: No Ravenna church's actual use is established. The present holdings and scholarly attribution do not establish local reception.

stages.label: Montecassino 271 early sacramentary lower layer
stages.scope: The identified early Gregorian sacramentary/readings stratum within a multiply reused codex, excluding its later missals and upper Gregory Dialogues.
stages.witness_label: Montecassino 271 [palimpsest old 2]: early Gregorian sacramentary and reading fragments
stages.summary: Catalogue and critical scholarship distinguish an early Mass-prayer/reading book from other layers of the present volume.

evidence.locus: CLA III 376 shelfmark palimpsest old 2; Date; Contents; Provenance
evidence.claim: The lower fragment dates 680-720 and was reused under Gregory Dialogues in the eleventh century.
The early sacramentary is item 71, separately from two X/XI-century missal strata.
The early book combined Mass prayers with readings, while Ravenna remains Gamber's supposition.

stages.limitations: Numeric date is one catalogue's interpretation, not a new palaeographic judgment; Usuarium gives 675-700. Complete original undertext, exact Canon scope and Ravenna use remain unproved. ELMSS 715 supplies the plotted 680–720 copying interpretation; Usuarium 6351 gives 675–700, while the indexed IRHT 599830 view gives 691–710 and Ravenna(?). The live IRHT delivery was inaccessible (https://liturgicum.irht.cnrs.fr/manuscrit/599830). These are qualified catalogue disagreements, not one harmonized date or a new palaeographic judgment.
stages.reception: No Ravenna church's actual use is established. The present holdings and scholarly attribution do not establish local reception.

stages.label: Munich Clm 29303(1 northern Italian lectionary strips
stages.date_label: Late-sixth-century ELMSS catalogue range 576–600; not a local-use chronology
stages.scope: Two horizontal strips from successive leaves of a Comes duplex. Hauke identifies partial Holy Week John 12:8–36 and Jeremiah 11:18–20; the CLA sample shows only selected verso surfaces. No annual-book extent is reconstructed.
stages.witness_label: Munich Clm 29303(1, formerly Clm 29155 c, CLA IX 1334
stages.summary: A physically identified northern Italian Mass-reading fragment; Usuarium’s linked current shelfmark points to a different Salzburg Gospel object.

evidence.locus: ELMSS 1835, CLA IX 1334, complete delivered sample image
evidence.claim: Late-sixth-century northern Italian lectionary fragments are identified; only selected original verso surfaces are shown.
The sixth-century two-strip Comes duplex Clm 29303(1 is distinct from ninth-century Salzburg Gospel fragments Clm 29270(8.

stages.limitations: The plotted 576–600 range is ELMSS’s catalogue interpretation; Hauke gives sixth century and Usuarium 575–600. The sample is not all surviving sides or a complete literal transcription. No Canon, annual Missal, distinct recension, historical parent, transition or text inheritance is asserted.
stages.reception: No Ravenna church’s actual use of these strips is established. A scholarly origin-table attribution, an old shelfmark alias and present Munich custody do not establish local reception.

gaps.missing: No original local-use or copying-place evidence identifies these fragments as a Ravenna recension.
gaps.next_source: Reopen Gamber CLLA646, 650-651, 659-660, 701 and named critical editions against full original leaves; obtain documented provenance and contemporary church-use evidence.
gaps.consequence: Keep the grouping attributed and separate from local reception. No ancestry, revision or text-inheritance edge follows.

gaps.missing: Complete Eucharistic-prayer extent and literal readings for 100A, the Stockholm-Wroclaw codex, Montecassino lower 2 and Ink.15370.
gaps.next_source: Dold 1923 pp. 10-11; Gamber 1960 pp. 455-460; Gamber 1958 pp. 111-126 and 1966 pp. 242-250; Dold 1943 pp. 1*-52*; Catella-Dell'Oro-Martini 2005 pp. 513-525. Collate surviving leaves before declaring anaphora coverage.
gaps.consequence: No anaphoras component or complete text is asserted by this dossier.

gaps.missing: Archive 011 remains an origin-unassigned 186-leaf missal-calendar; no original calendar, colophon, Canon, marginal use or provenance examined.

gaps.consequence: Archive 011 remains a holding-only candidate and receives no local-use stage.
